\section*{Question 4}

The figure above shows the graph of \(f^{\prime}\), the derivative of a twice-differentiable function \(f\), on the closed interval \(0 \leq x \leq 8\). The graph of \(f^{\prime}\) has horizontal tangent lines at \(x=1, x=3\), and \(x=5\). The areas of the regions between the graph of \(f^{\prime}\) and the \(x\)-axis are labeled in the figure. The function \(f\) is defined for all real numbers and satisfies \(f(8)=4\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find all values of \(x\) on the open interval \(0<x<8\) for which the function \(f\) has a local minimum. Justify your answer.
\item[(b)] Determine the absolute minimum value of \(f\) on the closed interval \(0 \leq x \leq 8\). Justify your answer.
\item[(c)] On what open intervals contained in \(0<x<8\) is the graph of \(f\) both concave down and increasing? Explain your reasoning.
\item[(d)] The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x)=(f(x))^{3}\). If \(f(3)=-\frac{5}{2}\), find the slope of the line tangent to the graph of \(g\) at \(x=3\).
\item[(a)] \(x=6\) is the only critical point at which \(f^{\prime}\) changes sign from negative to positive. Therefore, \(f\) has a local minimum at \(x=6\).
\item[(b)] From part (a), the absolute minimum occurs either at \(x=6\) or at an endpoint.
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(0) & =f(8)+\int_{8}^{0} f^{\prime}(x) d x \\
& =f(8)-\int_{0}^{8} f^{\prime}(x) d x=4-12=-8 \\
f(6) & =f(8)+\int_{8}^{6} f^{\prime}(x) d x \\
& =f(8)-\int_{6}^{8} f^{\prime}(x) d x=4-7=-3 \\
f(8) & =4
\end{aligned}
\]
The absolute minimum value of \(f\) on the closed interval [0,8] is -8.
\item[(c)] The graph of \(f\) is concave down and increasing on \(0<x<1\) and \(3<x<4\), because \(f^{\prime}\) is decreasing and positive on these intervals.
\item[(d)] \(g^{\prime}(x)=3[f(x)]^{2} \cdot f^{\prime}(x)\)
\[
g^{\prime}(3)=3[f(3)]^{2} \cdot f^{\prime}(3)=3\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right)^{2} \cdot 4=75
\]
\item[1] : answer with justification
\[
3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}
1: \text { considers } x=0 \text { and } x=6 \\
1: \text { answer } \\
1: \text { justification }
\end{array}\right.
\]
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { answer } \\ 1: \text { explanation }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: g^{\prime}(x) \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}
